answer: Require each reward identity to retain a distinct 10 GB replica encoded slowly under its key. A dataset could contain yarrow surveys from an oasis and ember-detection images. Unpredictable block queries demand compact proofs before deadlines shorter than rebuilding a replica; payment follows verified proofs. Fresh keys cannot reuse the same encoding. Operating k identities therefore requires roughly 10k GB of storage plus encoding work and ongoing query bandwidth, making extra reward slots costly.
